protections: P1: the default eval mode 'safe' must run filter and script expressions in the restricted AST interpreter (SafeEval), not in a native JS engine, in every build (node as well as browser).

P2: the restricted interpreter must not let an expression reach a code-constructing object (the Function constructor via the constructor/prototype chain), whatever the property name's shape or the lookup route (member access or identifier lookup).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: README says that in Node 'safe' 'has no effect and is equivalent to native as scripting is safe there', so vm.Script looks intentional.
evidence: src/jsonpath-node.js:4-5 (vm and safeVm both bound to Node's vm module)
src/jsonpath-node.js:7 (exported SafeScript is vm.Script)
src/jsonpath.js:165 (eval defaults to 'safe')
src/jsonpath.js:656-661 ('safe', true and undefined all dispatch to this.safeVm.Script)
src/jsonpath-browser.js:270-272 (only the browser build binds safeVm to the AST interpreter SafeScript)
README.md:179-183 (documents Node 'safe' as equivalent to native)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: SafeEval is an AST interpreter with no eval/Function call, so it looks safe by construction. Member access is a plain obj[prop] with no property restriction.
evidence: src/jsonpath-browser.js:143-147 (any property name, including prototype-chain names, is read with obj[prop])
src/jsonpath-browser.js:148-149 (function-valued results are returned bound, so constructor chains stay callable)
src/jsonpath-browser.js:166-170 (any reached function is called with evaluated arguments)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Once a check on the property name exists, a computed key looks like it is already covered because it evaluates to the same name. The check misses that the key may be a non-string value (an array) that is coerced only at obj[prop], or a string built at runtime (concatenation) rather than a literal.
evidence: src/jsonpath-browser.js:143-145 (computed key is the evaluated value of any expression, not coerced to string before use)
src/jsonpath-browser.js:163-165 (array expressions evaluate to arrays, which can serve as a computed key)
src/jsonpath-browser.js:76-104 (binary '+' builds strings at runtime, so a check on the AST literal misses them)
src/jsonpath-browser.js:147 (coercion of the key happens only at the property read)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Identifiers look like they resolve only to sandbox and @-variables ('is not defined' otherwise). But the 'in' test walks Object.prototype, so a bare identifier reaches inherited members such as 'constructor' (Object) and '__proto__' without any member-access name check.
evidence: src/jsonpath-browser.js:134-135 ('ast.name in subs' accepts inherited names and returns subs[name])
src/jsonpath-browser.js:200 (subs is a plain object literal spread from the sandbox, so it inherits Object.prototype)
src/jsonpath-browser.js:166-170 (static methods on the reached object are callable with string arguments, so a dangerous name can travel as a call argument rather than a member name)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Blocking calls or bound methods, or refusing every member named like a prototype property, looks like the safest fix, but method calls on data and JSON own keys must keep working.
evidence: test/test.examples.js:256 (@.match(/TION$/i) must work)
test/test.safe-eval.js:179 (array literal .includes(@property) must work)
test/test.eval.js:221 (@.category.toLowerCase() must work)
test/test.safe-eval.js:79-123 (sandbox functions must be callable)
src/jsonpath-browser.js:148-149 (methods are returned bound, which the above relies on)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Advisory payloads use the [?(...)] filter form. The dynamic-property form [(...)] and the nested-filter branch also reach _eval, so a string-level check placed only in the filter branch misses them.
evidence: src/jsonpath.js:432-436 (filter branch strips ?( ) and evaluates)
src/jsonpath.js:463-474 ([(expr)] branch calls this._eval with the raw loc)
src/jsonpath.js:438-453 (nested filter branch recurses via _trace into the same evaluator)
src/jsonpath.js:631-681 (single _eval sink for all routes)

masking: T1 masks T2/T3/T4 in the Node build. While Node 'safe' uses vm.Script (src/jsonpath-node.js:5), the SafeEval holes are reachable only through the browser build. Once T1 is fixed, they become the Node attack surface too.

src/jsonpath-browser.js:144 evaluates a computed key without subs. Fixing that (passing subs) widens T3: keys held in sandbox or assigned variables (src/jsonpath-browser.js:171-178) become usable as computed keys.

conflicts.what: A name denylist on member access, or a ban on calling bound methods, breaks @.match/.includes/.toLowerCase and sandbox functions (test/test.examples.js:256, test/test.safe-eval.js:179, test/test.eval.js:221). It also breaks JSON data that has an own key named 'constructor' unless the check exempts own properties.

Switching Node 'safe' to SafeEval changes documented Node behaviour (README.md:181-182). Expressions that vm accepts but SafeEval rejects (e.g. 'this', test/test.errors.js:70-79) start throwing under the default eval.
An own-property check in evalIdentifier must still resolve every sandbox key (including 'arguments', test/test.safe-eval.js:64-77) and the _$_ variables set at src/jsonpath.js:634-643.

fairness_risks: Test harness masks T1: test-helpers/node-env.js:7-14 imports both src/jsonpath-node.js and src/jsonpath-browser.js, and both mutate the same JSONPath.prototype from src/jsonpath.js (src/jsonpath-node.js:4-5, src/jsonpath-browser.js:266-272). The browser import wins, so 'Node vm' tests actually run SafeScript. A hidden T1 test must run in a separate process, or check src/jsonpath-node.js's binding directly or via dist/index-node-*.

JSONPath.cache (src/jsonpath.js:645-661, 693) is keyed by eval mode and code, not by implementation. A hidden test can be served a script compiled earlier in the same process by another build or binding. Clear the cache between cases.
JSON data with own keys named 'constructor' or '__proto__' is a legitimate shape. A test refusing those names regardless of ownership would penalise correct fixes that only block inherited lookups.
Method calls on values (.match, .includes, .toLowerCase, .length) and sandbox functions are must-keep-working. A test-visible rule 'no function calls' would contradict existing tests.
The README documents Node 'safe' as equivalent to native (README.md:181-182). The task report must make clear that Node default eval is in scope, or T1 is unfair.

design.why: Four independent fix sites with different reasons to dismiss: T1 (deepseek: the README says Node vm is safe; fix in src/jsonpath-node.js); T2+T3 (one member-access group, where T3 is a mimo how-type M8 shape: an array or runtime-built key evades a lexical or string-equality name check); T4 (deepseek/xhard: identifier lookup through the 'in' prototype walk reaches Object without any member name, a different fix site at src/jsonpath-browser.js:134); and T5 (mimo M11: method calls and own-key data must keep working, punishing over-hardening). T1 also masks the SafeEval holes in Node, so the stack rewards fixing both layers. T6 is left out as easy and absorbed by any SafeEval-level fix. Caveat: a single sink-side guard (refusing to call the Function constructor at src/jsonpath-browser.js:169) might collapse T2/T3/T4 into one group, unless hidden tests also cover native higher-order callbacks (e.g. Array.prototype.map) that invoke a reached constructor without going through evalCallExpression. See unverified.
